answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each new identity to burn a small, non-refundable amount of compute on a verifiable useful task before it may transact, such as solving a fresh optimization puzzle whose difficulty rises with every identity created from the same funding source. Like quartz forming slowly under pressure, reputation then accrues only through completed work, never bought at once. An attacker facing a dune of rising costs per fake identity finds mass creation uneconomic, while an honest agent pays once and keeps an ivory-clean record.
